These activities form a cycle of continuous improvement, as the following illustration shows: Minimizing resource use benefits your users and improves their perceptions of your app.
Decreasing overall memory use reduces the likelihood of iOS freeing your app’s memory in the background, and improves responsiveness when a user switches back to your app.
Reducing battery consumption and the use of power-hungry device features makes your app more reliable, and helps ensure that the rest of a person’s device is available when needed.
Maintaining low disk space usage allows a person to install and use more apps, and to keep more content on their device.
Doing so speeds up app and system upgrades, and reduces the iCloud storage space the system requires to create an iCloud backup of the device.

To thoroughly understand your app’s performance, combine information from multiple sources: Use the to view metrics for launch time, user-interface responsiveness, writes to storage, memory use, and energy use, as well as diagnostic reports for disk writes, crashes, and energy.

Use the information from your observations and your understanding of your app’s purpose and expected use patterns to spot the greatest opportunities for improvement.
For example, energy use associated with background-audio playing is probably not a problem for a podcast player, which users expect to play in the background.
